Customer (Megan Kerr): My bill jumped and I don't understand why. Did something change with my rate?
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Hi Megan Kerr, Vusi Jacobs here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Megan Kerr): I've been on the same rate for years, why is this changing now?
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Happy to explain it. Let me pull up your usage first.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Can you give me the account number from your bill, or the service address and the name on the account?
Customer (Megan Kerr): Sure, it's the house on the account, and the bill's in my name.

Customer (Megan Kerr): No idea. Can you look it up?
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Did you get the letter by mail or by email?
Customer (Megan Kerr): By mail, a couple of weeks ago.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Do you have any irrigation or shop meters on the same account?
Customer (Megan Kerr): No, just the house.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Let me take a look. I've pulled up the account, confirmed the Rate 1/Rate 2 threshold under the August 1 Phase 2 restructuring, and walked through what changed on this specific account.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Since August 1, Rate 1 covers accounts using under 4,000 GJ a year and Rate 2 covers larger users. The AUC approved it as Phase 2 of the rate restructuring.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): You're on Rate 1 since your annual usage is under 4,000 GJ, so the main change is the way the distribution charge is broken out on the bill — your total shouldn't move much. I've sent the AUC decision summary to your email so you have it on file.
Customer (Megan Kerr): So my total won't go up much?
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): It shouldn't. Most of this month's jump is colder weather, not the rate change.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Customer (Megan Kerr): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
